You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From bc22af74f271ef76b2e6f72f3941f91f0da3f5f8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Baron <jbaron@akamai.com>
Date: Thu, 5 May 2016 16:22:12 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mm: update min_free_kbytes from khugepaged after core
 initialization

Khugepaged attempts to raise min_free_kbytes if its set too low.
However, on boot khugepaged sets min_free_kbytes first from
subsys_initcall(), and then the mm 'core' over-rides min_free_kbytes
after from init_per_zone_wmark_min(), via a module_init() call.

Khugepaged used to use a late_initcall() to set min_free_kbytes (such
that it occurred after the core initialization), however this was
removed when the initialization of min_free_kbytes was integrated into
the starting of the khugepaged thread.

The fix here is simply to invoke the core initialization using a
core_initcall() instead of module_init(), such that the previous
initialization ordering is restored.  I didn't restore the
late_initcall() since start_stop_khugepaged() already sets
min_free_kbytes via set_recommended_min_free_kbytes().

This was noticed when we had a number of page allocation failures when
moving a workload to a kernel with this new initialization ordering.  On
an 8GB system this restores min_free_kbytes back to 67584 from 11365
when CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE=y is set and either
CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_ALWAYS=y or
CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_MADVISE=y.

Fixes: 79553da293d3 ("thp: cleanup khugepaged startup")
Signed-off-by: Jason Baron <jbaron@akamai.com>
Acked-by: Kirill A. Shutemov <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Acked-by: David Rientjes <rientjes@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 59de90d5d3a3..c1069efcc4d7 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -6485,7 +6485,7 @@ int __meminit init_per_zone_wmark_min(void)
 	setup_per_zone_inactive_ratio();
 	return 0;
 }
-module_init(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
+core_initcall(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
 
 /*
  * min_free_kbytes_sysctl_handler - just a wrapper around proc_dointvec() so
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `mm/page_alloc.c`**
   - The function `init_per_zone_wmark_min()` was changed from being registered with `module_init()` to `core_initcall()`. This change alters the initialization order of the function, ensuring that it is called during the core initialization phase rather than as part of module initialization.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `mm/page_alloc.c` restores the previous initialization order for `min_free_kbytes`, which is crucial for the proper functioning of the `khugepaged` mechanism. By using `core_initcall()`, the initialization of `min_free_kbytes` occurs after the core memory management setup, preventing page allocation failures that were observed when the workload was moved to a kernel with the new initialization order. This change directly addresses the issue of low `min_free_kbytes` values that were causing allocation failures, thereby improving system stability and performance when using transparent huge pages.

mm: update min_free_kbytes from khugepaged after core
 initialization

Khugepaged attempts to raise min_free_kbytes if its set too low.
However, on boot khugepaged sets min_free_kbytes first from
subsys_initcall(), and then the mm 'core' over-rides min_free_kbytes
after from init_per_zone_wmark_min(), via a module_init() call.

Khugepaged used to use a late_initcall() to set min_free_kbytes (such
that it occurred after the core initialization), however this was
removed when the initialization of min_free_kbytes was integrated into
the starting of the khugepaged thread.

The fix here is simply to invoke the core initialization using a
core_initcall() instead of module_init(), such that the previous
initialization ordering is restored.  I didn't restore the
late_initcall() since start_stop_khugepaged() already sets
min_free_kbytes via set_recommended_min_free_kbytes().

This was noticed when we had a number of page allocation failures when
moving a workload to a kernel with this new initialization ordering.  On
an 8GB system this restores min_free_kbytes back to 67584 from 11365
when CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE=y is set and either
CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_ALWAYS=y or
CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE_MADVISE=y.

Fixes: 79553da293d3 ("thp: cleanup khugepaged startup")
Signed-off-by: Jason Baron <jbaron@akamai.com>
Acked-by: Kirill A. Shutemov <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Acked-by: David Rientjes <rientjes@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the improper initialization order of `min_free_kbytes`, which was set too low during the boot process. The `khugepaged` component attempted to raise `min_free_kbytes` after its initial setting, but this was overridden by the core memory management initialization that occurred later. This led to insufficient memory being available for page allocations, resulting in allocation failures when workloads were moved to the kernel with the new initialization order.

Here is the patch:
 }
-module_init(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
+core_initcall(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
 
 /*
  * min_free_kbytes_sysctl_handler - just a wrapper around proc_dointvec() so
  *	that we can call two helper functions whenever min_free_kbytes
  *	changes.
  */
 int min_free_kbytes_sysctl_handler(struct ctl_table *table, int write,
 	void __user *buffer, size_t *length, loff_t *ppos)
 {
 	int rc;
 
 	rc = proc_dointvec_minmax(table, write, buffer, length, ppos);
 	if (rc)
 		return rc;
 
 	if (write) {
 		user_min_free_kbytes = min_free_kbytes;
 		setup_per_zone_wmarks();
 	}
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
module_init(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
```
Reason:
The `module_init()` call for `init_per_zone_wmark_min` initializes `min_free_kbytes` too late in the boot process, overriding the earlier setting by `khugepaged`, which attempts to raise `min_free_kbytes`. This results in `min_free_kbytes` being set too low, causing page allocation failures.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
core_initcall(init_per_zone_wmark_min)
```
Reason:
Changing `module_init()` to `core_initcall()` ensures that `init_per_zone_wmark_min` is called earlier in the initialization sequence, before `khugepaged` sets `min_free_kbytes`. This restores the proper initialization order, preventing the low setting of `min_free_kbytes` and thus avoiding page allocation failures.
